expectations.text: Keyboard interaction and focus management are implemented, not just mouse clicks
expectations.evidence: DropdownMenu.tsx has onTriggerKeyDown (ArrowDown/ArrowUp open with first/last focus) and onMenuKeyDown (ArrowUp/Down wrap, Home, End, Escape, Tab). close(true) returns focus to the trigger. A useEffect focuses the first or last enabled item on open. Disabled items are excluded from navigation.

expectations.text: ARIA roles or semantic elements are used correctly
expectations.evidence: The trigger is a real <button> with aria-haspopup="menu", aria-expanded and aria-controls (a useId id). The list is <ul role="menu" aria-label>. Each <li> has role="none" and holds a <button role="menuitem" tabIndex={-1}>. The disabled attribute is used for disabled items. This matches the WAI-ARIA menu button pattern.

expectations.text: Component state is managed deliberately rather than ad hoc
expectations.evidence: A single isOpen useState drives the menu. A pendingFocus ref records which item to focus after render. The open() and close(returnFocus) helpers centralize transitions. Effects handle focus-on-open and outside-click, and clean up their listeners. Refs are used for the DOM nodes.
